title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378W (Chief Executive and his functions)

content.overview: Every Producer Company shall have a full-time Chief Executive, by whatever name called, appointed by the Board from amongst persons other than Members. The Chief Executive is an ex officio director who does not retire by rotation. Qualifications, experience and terms of service are determined by the Board (save as otherwise in the articles). The Chief Executive is entrusted with substantial powers of management as the Board may determine, including routine administration, operation of bank accounts (subject to Board approval), and the other functions listed in the section. The Chief Executive manages the affairs of the Producer Company under the general superintendence, direction and control of the Board and is accountable for the performance of the Company.
content.glance: Full-time Chief Executive (non-Member), ex officio non-retiring director, substantial management powers under Board control, accountable for company performance.
content.study: Section 378W requires every Producer Company to have a full-time Chief Executive appointed by the Board from outside the membership. The Chief Executive is an ex officio director who does not retire by rotation, holds substantial management powers as determined by the Board, and remains under Board superintendence and control while being accountable for company performance.
